title: CropWatch Rwanda
subtitle: Agricultural data for Rwanda, from 2018 to 2026, cleaned and matched.
home_lead: This page shows data that has already been cleaned. One crop row is one crop on a sampled plot. It is not the national total.
not_all: Coffee, tea, and fodder still have no market price. Drying days are still not listed, so the app does not warn about rain during drying. Export lines for 2026 are not in the file. Vegetation is one number for each district and each year.
safe_lead: These crops use the same product in the survey and in the price list. Bush bean and climbing bean are both dry beans, so they share one price. They are still two crops. Do not add their harvests together and call it one crop.
close_lead: These names look related. They stay apart so flour is not treated as the harvest, and paddy rice is not treated as rice you buy to cook.
unmatched_lead: These survey crops have no price row we can trust. Many are fodder, spices, or crops written as other.
season_lead: NISR uses three seasons. The same months are used for the whole country.
calendar_lead: For maize and sorghum, FAO published one national calendar in 2015. Planting and harvest months below come from that calendar. Drying days were not published, so that column is empty.
zone_lead: This second calendar comes from the FAO file you added. It gives planting and harvest for 12 crops in 6 farming zones. A zone is not the same as a district. Drying days are still empty.
rain_lead: This compares the rain in a month with the usual rain for that same month. Usual means the average from 2018 to 2025. A negative difference means the month was drier than usual.
watch_lead: Usual maize yield is the past average. Prices are compared only in the same unit. Formal exports are maize HS 1005 through 2025.
watch_drier: Rain this season is {pct:.0f}% below usual. The usual maize yield here is {yield_kg:.0f} kg per hectare. That is the past average, not the harvest of this season.
watch_wetter: Rain this season is {pct:.0f}% above usual. The usual maize yield here is {yield_kg:.0f} kg per hectare. That is the past average, not the harvest of this season.
watch_close: Rain this season is close to usual ({pct:.0f}%). The usual maize yield here is {yield_kg:.0f} kg per hectare. That is the past average, not the harvest of this season.
price_here: The latest maize price in this district is {price:.0f} RWF per kg, on {date}. It is a market price.
price_national: This district has no maize price in 2025 or 2026. On {date}, the markets that did report maize averaged {price:.0f} RWF per kg.
veg_line: For the whole of {year}, the vegetation number is {now:.2f}. The usual number for 2018–2025 is {usual:.2f}. This is the year, not the season.
export_lead: These are formal maize exports. The World total is not added to the countries. There is no 2026 file.
export_partners: Top partners in the latest year
how_1: The survey files from 2018 to 2025 were read and stacked. One row is one crop on a plot. We did not delete odd rows. We did not change the area units. For 2018 and 2019 the plot weight is not on the crop file, so those years cannot be turned into a national total from this file alone.
how_2: The price file is the WFP market list. The last price date is 15 March 2026. We compare prices only when the unit is the same.
how_3: Rain is monthly, for all 30 districts, from January 2018 through August 2026.
how_4: Crop names were matched by reading both lists. A pair is marked safe only when it is the same product. The trade heading is the international product group, not a six-digit code from a new download.
how_5: Kinyarwanda on this app is the everyday name of the crop or the season. District names stay as they are, because they are place names. Province names use the Kinyarwanda names: Iburasirazuba, Iburengerazuba, Amajyaruguru, Amajyepfo, and Umujyi wa Kigali.
how_6: The app can be read in Kinyarwanda for the data that matched. It does not invent a match for the crops that have no price.
how_7: The soil page uses Season A 2022 only. That is the last year these questions are written in words and the plot weight is on the file. A plot with no follow-up answer, after the farmer said the practice was not used on any plot, counts as no. Season B is not added to Season A. Moderate erosion is water running over the soil. Severe erosion is rills, gullies, or a landslide. Splash and wind stay out of that share.
soil_lead: Season A 2022 erosion, protection, and fertilizer shares. These numbers describe surveyed plots, not every farm.
soil_sentence: In Season A 2022, {concern:.0f}% of the sampled plots had moderate or severe erosion. {severe:.0f}% were severe: rills, gullies, or a landslide. {protected:.0f}% had some protection against erosion. {organic:.0f}% used organic fertilizer. {inorganic:.0f}% used inorganic fertilizer.
soil_short: Of the plots that used organic fertilizer, {short:.0f}% said the amount was not enough.
soil_rain_drier: Season B 2026 rain here is {pct:.0f}% below usual ({rain:.0f} mm, compared with {usual:.0f} mm). The usual maize yield is {yield_kg:.0f} kg per hectare. The soil figures are from 2022. The rain is from 2026.
soil_rain_wetter: Season B 2026 rain here is {pct:.0f}% above usual ({rain:.0f} mm, compared with {usual:.0f} mm). The usual maize yield is {yield_kg:.0f} kg per hectare. The soil figures are from 2022. The rain is from 2026.
soil_rain_close: Season B 2026 rain here is close to usual ({pct:.0f}%, {rain:.0f} mm compared with {usual:.0f} mm). The usual maize yield is {yield_kg:.0f} kg per hectare. The soil figures are from 2022. The rain is from 2026.
hero_title: See which districts started this season drier than usual — and almost without irrigation.
hero_lead: CropWatch Rwanda is a season desk for farming. It joins official plot surveys with rain and a seven-day forecast, then names a next step you can read. It does not forecast this season’s harvest.
what_lead: The challenge is small-scale irrigation. A rain-based yield model was tested and lost to the past district average, so that forecast stays out.
card_fresh_body: Rain since 1 September 2026 is from Open-Meteo. Usual September–October is CHIRPS 2018–2025. Those are two products. The gap is a signal, not a millimetre-perfect difference.
card_rule_body: An irrigation alert means rain so far is at least 10% below usual, and fewer than 10% of sampled plots were irrigated in Season A 2022.
card_action_body: Prioritise watering cans, treadle pumps, and marshland in the alert districts. This is not a design for a dam.
logic_1: Irrigation alert: rain since 1 September is 10% or more below usual September–October, and fewer than 10% of Season A 2022 plots were irrigated.
logic_2: Irrigate this week: that irrigation alert, and the next seven days total less than 10 mm.
logic_3: Soil rain: at least 20% of plots had moderate or severe erosion, protection is under 80%, and any of the next seven days is 15 mm or more.
logic_4: The yield number on a district page is the past maize average. It is not this season's harvest.
alerts_title: Where this season needs water or soil care
alerts_lead: Colour is the alert. Click a district on the map, or pick one below, to see rain versus usual, irrigation on sampled plots, and the next seven days.
alert_irrigation_gap: {district}: rain so far is {pct:.0f}% below usual. Only {irrig:.1f}% of sampled plots were irrigated in Season A 2022. Rain is forecast this week ({week:.0f} mm). Catch it if you can, and keep a watering plan if it misses your plots.
alert_irrigate_now: {district}: the season is behind, few plots have irrigation, and the next seven days look dry ({week:.0f} mm). Water now if you can.
alert_soil_rain: {district}: {concern:.0f}% of plots had moderate or severe erosion, protection is {protected:.0f}%, and heavy rain is forecast this week. Check ditches and grass strips before it arrives.
alert_dry_watch: {district}: rain so far is {pct:.0f}% below usual. Irrigation is {irrig:.1f}%. Watch the seven-day forecast.
alert_soil_watch: {district}: {concern:.0f}% of plots had moderate or severe erosion, and protection is {protected:.0f}%. Heavy rain is not the main forecast this week, but the ditches still matter.
alert_stable: {district}: rain so far is close to or above usual. Irrigation is still rare ({irrig:.1f}%). No irrigation alert.
meta_line: This season {now:.0f} mm · usual Sep–Oct {usual:.0f} mm · next 7 days {week:.0f} mm
week_lead: Open-Meteo daily rain at the district midpoint. This is a weather forecast, not a harvest forecast.
action_irrigation: Action: small-scale irrigation. Watering cans, treadle pumps, and marshland. Not a dam.
action_soil: Action: soil protection. Ditches, grass strips, and terraces before the next heavy rain.
action_stable: No irrigation alert in this district today. Keep reading the seven-day forecast.
how_8: Open-Meteo supplies the rain since 1 September 2026 and the next seven days, using the midpoint of each district from the NISR shapefile. Usual September–October rain is CHIRPS 2018–2025. Irrigation and soil shares are Season A 2022 survey plots, weighted. A rain-based maize yield model was tested and lost to the past district average, so this app ships the alert rule instead of that forecast.
footer_blurb: A season desk for Rwandan farming, from NISR plots, CHIRPS usual rain, and Open-Meteo.
footer_copy: NISR 2026 Big Data Hackathon · Track 1 Agricultural Productivity
sim_title: What if irrigation or compost had been different in 2022?
sim_lead: Sliders use the 2022 within-district plot gap. They are hypothetical. This is not a MINAGRI subsidy calculator and not a 2026 harvest.
sim_irrig_slider: Simulate small-scale irrigation expansion (percentage points of plots)
sim_organic_slider: Simulate organic fertilizer shortage reduction (percentage points)
sim_irrig_help: Moves the irrigated share of Season A 2022 plots up by this many points. The kg/ha figure is the 2022 within-district gap, not a subsidy payment.
sim_organic_help: Cuts the share of organic-using plots that said the amount was not enough. The kg/ha figure is the 2022 within-district gap.
sim_protect_slider: Anti-erosion protection (not used as a yield lever)
sim_policy_note: NST2 and MINAGRI's Small-Scale Irrigation Technology (SSIT) programme name irrigation and soil fertility as productivity tools. MINAGRI has described a 50% SSIT subsidy on approved equipment. This screen is not an official NST2 score, not a subsidy calculator, and not this season's harvest.
sim_body: In {district}, irrigated maize plots yielded about {irrig_gap:.0f} kg/ha more than other plots in the same district. Plots that said organic fertilizer was not enough yielded about {short_gap:.0f} kg/ha less. Adding {d_irrig:.0f} points of irrigation and cutting the shortage share by {d_short:.0f} points is associated with {gain:.0f} kg/ha ({pct:+.1f}%).
sim_protect_note: Plots with anti-erosion works yielded less in the same district in 2022, likely because those plots sit on steeper land. Protection is not used here as a yield gain.
benchmark_title: Season A 2022 — source of the what-if sliders
benchmark_lead: 11,148 maize plots, 30 districts. Rain-only loses to the district mean. A forest and gradient boosting beat that mean on held-out plots. Other years and seasons are scored in the tables above. None of these is a 2026 harvest.
feat_title: Pooled forest importance (not the same as the what-if gap)
feat_veg: District NDRE in the interview year
map_lead: Hover or click a district for rain vs usual, the irrigated share of Season A 2022 plots, and the next seven days of rain. Use the list below to open the district board.
map_legend: Red: irrigate this week · Orange: irrigation gap · Yellow: soil watch · Green: no alert
map_missing: The district map file is not on disk. Run python src/model_yield.py to build districts.geojson from the NISR shapefile.
how_9: Every SAS maize A/B file from 2018–2026 was read. Plot-level models need yield (native or production/area), plot_weight, and a join to practice and fertilizer. That holds for 2022 A/B, 2023 A/B, and 2025 A. 2025 B has too few plots. 2018–2019 lack plot_weight. 2024 has production without area. 2026 is published tables. 2020–2021 have yield and weight, but the irrigation join drops them; they still enter the district-season rain+NDRE panel. Shuffled CV, grouped-by-district CV, and leave-one-year-out are all reported. The what-if sliders use Season A 2022 within-district OLS, not a harvest forecast. s4q8 and s4q11 are machines, not fertilizer.
records_title: Survey crop rows by year and season
records_note: These are interview rows, not tonnes for the whole country.
about_lead: A student project for the NISR 2026 Big Data Hackathon, Track 1. It is a season desk, not an official NISR or MINAGRI product.
about_body: CropWatch shows which of Rwanda’s 30 districts started Season A 2026 drier than usual, with little irrigation on sampled plots. It uses NISR survey files, CHIRPS usual rain, Open-Meteo rain and the week ahead, and — for four districts — NASA POWER weather at the midpoint.
about_farmer: Farmer: this week's rain, a demo SMS for a basic phone, and advice in plain words.
about_agro: Agronomist: map layers for rain, irrigation, soil, and NDRE, plus the soil page.
about_policy: Policymaker: the 2022 plot gap and an SSIT kit class by farm size. There is no official pump price in these files.
about_ai: Advice uses this district's tables. If a Groq or Gemini key is present, Llama 3.1 or Gemini Flash writes the sentences. If not, the same numbers are returned as short rules. No yield is invented.
chat_hello: Hello. I can help with {district}. Rain so far is {rain:.0f}% versus usual, and the next seven days are {week:.0f} mm. {irrig:.1f}% of Season A 2022 plots were irrigated. Ask about rain, soil, maize price, or an irrigation kit class.
chat_llm_on: Longer answers use a free Groq Llama 3.1 key. The numbers still come from this district's files.
chat_llm_off: No cloud key is set, so replies stay on the district tables. For fuller sentences add a free Groq key: GROQ_API_KEY in .streamlit/secrets.toml.
role_all_lead: All tools stay visible. Pick a desk to put the next step first.
role_farmer_lead: A farmer desk: this week's rain, a demo SMS for a basic phone, and advice in plain words. It is not a MINAGRI broadcast.
role_agronomist_lead: An agronomist desk: switch the map layer, read soil and irrigation shares, and compare Sentinel NDRE with the national line.
role_policy_lead: A policymaker desk: the 2022 plot gap, a kit class by farm size, and the stated SSIT 50% co-share. There is no official price list in these files.
layer_lead: One layer colours the 30 districts. The numbers are the same files as the table.
filter_rain: Show districts this dry or drier (% vs usual)
ndre_lead: One vegetation number per district and year. The grey line is the mean of all 30 districts. Season A 2019 and 2023 were drier than usual in CHIRPS; NDRE also dipped then. 2026 is the lowest national mean in this file.
sms_note: This is a mock-up of a message a sector could send to a basic phone. CropWatch does not send SMS. It is not an official MINAGRI text.
sms_body: CropWatch: {district} rain so far is {pct:.0f}% below usual. Next 7 days {week:.0f} mm. If plots are rain-fed, water with cans or a treadle pump. Dial *801# on this screen to walk through the demo. Not a MINAGRI broadcast.
ussd_home:
1 Weather alert
2 Soil and ditches
3 SSIT kit class
0 Back
ussd_weather: {district}: rain {pct:.0f}% vs usual. Week {week:.0f} mm. Irrigated plots {irrig:.1f}%.
ussd_soil: {district}: moderate/severe erosion {concern:.0f}%. Protection {protected:.0f}%. Check ditches before a 15 mm day.
ussd_kit: SSIT is a MINAGRI 50% co-share on approved equipment. This demo does not place an order and has no official pump price.
ssit_lead: Pick a plot size. The kit class follows common SSIT groups (treadle, solar drip, motor pump). Yield protection uses the 2022 maize irrigation gap in the same district. Equipment RWF is not in these files, so it is not quoted.
ssit_badge: Policy context: MINAGRI SSIT 50% co-share on approved equipment (NST2). Not an official quote.
ssit_protect: Associated maize protection (kg on this plot)
ssit_value: That grain at the latest maize price (RWF)
ssit_other_crop: This file has a maize yield gap. Vegetables, beans, and potato keep the same kit class; they do not get a invented kg/ha.
ssit_no_price: This district has no 2025–2026 maize price row. The national maize average on {date} is used for the RWF line.
chat_lead: Answers use this district’s tables. Without an API key the replies are short rules, not a chat invention.
chat_pill_week: What should farmers do this week?
chat_pill_kit: What irrigation kit class fits here?
chat_pill_soil: How do I protect the soil?
chat_week_head: {district}: rain so far is {rain:.0f}% vs usual. Next 7 days {week:.0f} mm. Season A 2022 irrigated plots {irrig:.1f}%.
chat_week_irrig: This is an irrigation-gap pattern: the season is behind and almost no sampled plots were irrigated. Watering cans, treadle pumps, and marshland are the next step named on Alerts. Not a dam.
chat_week_dryweek: The coming week is dry. Keep a watering plan if you can.
chat_week_ok: Rain so far is close to usual, or irrigation is not the binding alert. Keep reading the seven-day forecast.
chat_week_soil: Erosion concern is high and protection is incomplete, with a heavy day in the forecast. Check ditches and grass strips.
chat_week_ssit: MINAGRI SSIT names a 50% co-share on approved small-scale irrigation equipment. Ask the sector agronomist for the current list. This app does not file a request.
chat_soil: {district}: {concern:.0f}% of Season A 2022 plots had moderate or severe erosion. {protected:.0f}% had some protection.
chat_soil_act: Before the next heavy rain: ditches, grass strips (urubingo), and compost on bare soil. Terraces are already on many steep plots; they are not used here as a yield slider.
chat_soil_ok: Protection is relatively high in the 2022 sample. Keep the ditches clear.
chat_kit: {district}: only {irrig:.1f}% of Season A 2022 plots were irrigated. For about {ha:.1f} ha, the SSIT-style class is: {name}.
chat_kit_policy: That is a size class, not a MINAGRI invoice. The 50% co-share applies to approved equipment on the official list, which is not in this repository.
chat_price_here: {district} maize retail was {price:.0f} RWF/kg on {date} (WFP, same unit).
chat_price_national: {district} has no maize price in 2025–2026. Markets that did report averaged {price:.0f} RWF/kg on {date}.
chat_price_note: Compare prices only in the same unit. This is a market price, not a farm-gate promise.
chat_calendar: NISR seasons: A September–February, B March–June, C July–September. FAO also published planting months for maize and sorghum; drying days were not in that file.
chat_yield: {district} usual maize yield is {yield_kg:.0f} kg/ha. That is the past average, not this season's harvest. Irrigated 2022 plots in the same district yielded about 365 kg/ha more.
chat_veg: {district} Sentinel NDRE in 2026 is {now:.3f}. The 2018–2025 mean for this district is {usual:.3f}. One number per year, not a daily crop map.
chat_empty: Ask about rain, irrigation, soil, price, or the kit class for this district.
home_challenge_lead: In Season A 2022 only 2.2% of NISR survey plots were irrigated. When this Season A starts drier than usual, those plots have little to fall back on. CropWatch does not invent a bigger national crisis number than that survey share.
home_ch_1: Dependence on rainfall, and a live week that can still miss the plot.
home_ch_2: Soil erosion and incomplete protection on sampled plots (Season A 2022).
home_ch_3: Limited visibility of this season until harvest is in — so the app does not forecast that harvest.
home_ch_4: Survey, climate, satellite, and price files that do not join themselves.
home_ch_5: Statistics that stay in tables unless someone names a next step: watering cans, ditches, or a kit class.
home_how_title: A rule you can read, not a silent model.
home_how_1: Rain since 1 September 2026 against usual September–October (2018–2025). Two rain products, so the gap is a signal.
home_how_2: Share of Season A 2022 sampled plots that were irrigated. Under 10% plus a dry start is an irrigation gap.
home_how_3: Seven-day rain versus maize water demand. If the week is also dry, the label becomes irrigate this week.
home_how_4: A printed alert rule: rain ≥10% below usual Sep–Oct and irrigated share under 10% is an irrigation gap. Soil-rain needs erosion, weak protection, and a ≥15 mm day.
home_how_5: District boards, a map, a what-if on 2022 plot gaps, an SSIT kit class by farm size, and advice in English or Kinyarwanda. Not a MINAGRI order form.
home_mod_title: One desk, three kinds of reader.
home_mod_alerts: Climate Alerts — rainfall versus usual, a seven-day forecast, and irrigation context on a district map.
home_mod_soil: Soil & Conservation — Season A 2022 erosion, terracing/protection, organic and inorganic fertilizer.
home_mod_season: Season Watch — rain, usual maize yield, WFP price, NDRE, and formal maize exports.
home_mod_sim: Policy Simulator — 2022 within-district kg/ha gaps and an SSIT size class. Hypothetical, labelled as such.
home_mod_advise: Advise — a district chat grounded in the same tables. Groq is optional.
home_nat_title: Thirty districts, one rule, no silent model.
home_nat_body: District-level shares help a planner see where this Season A started drier than usual and where sampled irrigation is rare. That is a priority signal for small-scale water, not a ranking of districts as failures. Open the Dashboard for the current counts.
home_ev_title: Every important number has a file, a year, and a limit.
home_ev_body: Data Sources details verified national and global publishers. Methodology documents survey weighting, satellite reanalysis, and machine learning benchmarks. About details strategic alignment with NST2 and PSTA 5 priorities.
home_nst_title: NST2 and Vision 2050 as policy context, not an official score.
home_nst_body: Track 1 asks for agricultural productivity, including water and soil. CropWatch maps onto small-scale irrigation and conservation using NISR plots plus climate files. MINAGRI SSIT is named as the 50% co-share programme on approved equipment. This app does not issue that subsidy and does not score NST2.
home_final_body: You do not need to know the files. Pick a district you know, read the label, then read why.
dash_lead: National counts at the top. Then choose a district to see the label, the reason, and this week’s rain. Usual maize yield is the past average, not this harvest.
dash_risk_title: How many districts have each label
dash_profile_lead: Historical soil and irrigation shares are Season A 2022. Rain and the week are 2026. They are not the same year.
dash_status_api: Open-Meteo is not called on this page view
export_note: CSV and HTML include source, units, and the printed alert rule. They are not a government certificate.
why_irrigation_gap: Irrigation gap: rain since 1 September 2026 is at least 10% below usual September–October (CHIRPS 2018–2025), and fewer than 10% of Season A 2022 sampled plots were irrigated (NISR SAS, plot-weighted).
why_irrigate_now: Irrigate this week: the irrigation-gap rule, and the next seven Open-Meteo days total less than 10 mm.
why_soil_rain: Soil and rain: at least 20% of Season A 2022 plots had moderate or severe erosion, protection under 80%, and any of the next seven days is 15 mm or more.
why_soil_watch: Soil watch: erosion concern and protection cross the soil thresholds, but the week is not the heavy-rain trigger.
why_dry_watch: Dry start: rain is behind usual, but the irrigated-share test for an irrigation gap is not the binding line in this row.
why_stable: No irrigation or soil-rain alert on the printed rule. Irrigation can still be rare. Keep reading the seven-day forecast.
why_sources: Sources: NISR SAS Season A 2022; CHIRPS usual Sep–Oct 2018–2025; Open-Meteo archive since 1 Sep 2026 and 7-day forecast. CHIRPS and Open-Meteo are two products.
src_lead: Each source has a publisher, a time window, and a limit. Nothing here is a field visit.
src_live: Live API (written into a table when alerts are prepared)
method_lead: How plots were stacked, how the alert rule is written, and how the maize model was scored out of sample. The model is not this season’s harvest.
gl_forecast: Agricultural forecast — igenamiterere ry'ubuhinzi (this app does not ship a harvest forecast)
about_obj_body: Name districts where this Season A started drier than usual and sampled irrigation is rare. Show soil conservation from Season A 2022. Keep yield language honest: past average and 2022 plot gaps, not 2026 harvest.
footer_tagline: Read the season. Then choose a district.
footer_disclaimer: Alert labels and model gaps are decision-support. They are not guaranteed farm outcomes and not an official NISR, MINAGRI, or NST2 product.
footer_privacy: No login is required for these public tables. Optional Groq/Gemini keys stay in server secrets and are not shown in the browser.
footer_limitations: Data limitations: 2026 SAS is published tables not plots; WFP maize kg is sparse; no 2026 Comtrade file; FAO drying days were never published; CHIRPS ≠ Open-Meteo.
footer_ack: Data: NISR SAS and shapefile; CHIRPS; Open-Meteo; Sentinel NDRE; WFP prices; UN Comtrade; FAO calendars. NASA POWER is used for four pilot districts only.
sim_assump: This scenario is hypothetical. It applies 2022 within-district plot gaps to a change in shares. Validation is the out-of-sample table on Methodology. It is not proven government policy.
alerts_explain: A rainfall anomaly is this Season A rain so far minus usual September–October (CHIRPS 2018–2025), as a percent of usual. Forecast rain and ET0 are Open-Meteo. Irrigation and erosion context is Season A 2022. Maize water demand uses FAO-56 Kc, not a field visit.
soil_explain: Erosion and protection come from Season A 2022 practice questions, plot-weighted. Terraces and ditches sit in the protection share. Fertilizer is the fertilizer file (s3q*), not machines (s4q8/s4q11).
watch_explain: Rain, past maize yield, NDRE, and the maize price are complementary. They are not one harvest number. Yield is the past district-season average.
empty_district: No row for this filter. Widen the rain slider or choose All districts.
cover_title: Which SAS years enter the maize model
cover_lead: Every season file was read. Plot-level kg/ha needs production and harvested area (or a native yield), plot_weight, then a join to practice and fertilizer on year, season, district, segment, household, and plot. Years that fail that test are listed here, not dropped in silence.
slice_title: Plot-level scores by year and season
slice_lead: Each row is a separate 3-fold shuffled test on that season’s maize plots. Rain-only, district mean, and a random forest of practices + rain + NDRE. The forest beating the district mean means practices add a little information. It is not a 2026 harvest.
pooled_lead: 28,042 maize plots from seasons that joined. Shuffled 5-fold can leak neighbouring plots in the same district. Grouped-by-district CV holds out whole districts — the stricter test of whether practices travel to a new place.
panel_lead: When the plot join is incomplete, district maize means still exist for 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023 and 2025. Leave-one-year-out tests whether rain and NDRE predict a year the model never saw. Negative R² means they do not.
sim_source_note: The what-if sliders still use Season A 2022 within-district OLS. That year has native yield, 11,148 plots, and 30 districts. Other years are scored above so the 2022 gap is not treated as the only result. None of this is this season’s harvest.
climate_lead: These classes use Open-Meteo ET0, a maize Kc from FAO-56, and the Season A rain gap. They are not a harvest forecast and not NASA SMAP soil moisture.
intel_used_body: NISR SAS Season A 2022 irrigation and erosion shares (plot-weighted); CHIRPS usual Sep–Oct 2018–2025; Open-Meteo archive rain and FAO-56 ET0 since 1 Sep 2026; Open-Meteo 7-day forecast. Sentinel NDRE is a district-year index, not this week’s crop.
intel_method_body: Irrigation gap if rain is ≥10% below usual and irrigated plots are under 10%. Soil-rain if erosion concern ≥20%, protection <80%, and any forecast day ≥15 mm. FAO-56: ETc = ET0 × Kc. Effective rain is 60% of daily rain ≤5 mm, else 80%. Week water balance = Pe − ETc.
intel_limits_body: Kc uses an assumed 15 Sep 2026 plant date from the FAO GIEWS Season A window, not a field visit. Stored soil water is unknown. NASA POWER and SMAP are named in the proposal and not connected. This is decision-support, not a MINAGRI order.
intel_balance: This week: effective rain {pe:.0f} mm minus maize ETc {etc:.0f} mm = {bal:+.0f} mm (Kc {kc:.2f}, stage {stage}). Atmospheric water balance, not soil moisture on the plot.
home_mod_water: FAO-56 maize water demand from Open-Meteo ET0 × crop coefficient, compared with this week’s rain. Not a farm soil-moisture sensor.
how_10: FAO-56 maize water: Open-Meteo daily ET0 at the district midpoint, Kc from FAO-56 Table 12 (grain maize 0.30 / 1.20 / 0.60) and tropical stage lengths Table 11 (20/35/40/30 days). Assumed plant date 15 September 2026 from the FAO GIEWS Season A planting window. Effective rain is a simple 60%/80% rule. Climate classes are Normal monitoring, Rainfall watch, Potential water stress, Excess rainfall watch, and Agronomist assessment. NASA POWER and NASA SMAP are listed as not connected. The class is not a harvest, not a landslide warning, and not a field soil-moisture reading.
pilot_note: Proposal pilot districts for later field checks: Bugesera, Nyagatare, Musanze, Nyaruguru. This build already covers all 30 districts.
gl_etc: Crop evapotranspiration (ETc) — amazi igihingwa gikoresha (ET0 × Kc)
gl_et0: Reference evapotranspiration (ET0) — Open-Meteo FAO-56 atmospheric water demand
pilot_lead: Bugesera, Nyagatare, Musanze and Nyaruguru. Same rule as the other 26 districts, plus NASA POWER temperature and solar at the midpoint.
pilot_body: This is the working prototype of the six-month proposal. All 30 districts stay on Overview and Alerts. NASA SMAP is not connected. POWER rain is not added to CHIRPS.
pilot_limits: NASA POWER is a satellite-model weather product at one point per district, 1 Sep–29 Oct 2026. It is not a farm sensor and not soil moisture. The assumed maize plant date is 15 Sep 2026.

guide_alerts_map_desc: This interactive map visualizes all 30 districts of Rwanda categorized by agroclimatic alert severity. Red represents an urgent Irrigation Gap (severe rainfall deficit combined with low irrigation coverage), Amber indicates Watch Closely (moderate deficit or critical phenological stage), and Green denotes Stable Soil Moisture. Toggle between layers (Alerts, Climate Classes, Rainfall Deficit, Irrigation Share, Soil Risk, and Vegetation NDRE) to inspect spatial patterns. Click any district polygon to inspect detailed meteorological and agricultural parameters.
guide_alerts_table_desc: Districts are prioritized by cumulative seasonal rainfall deviation relative to the long-term 1981-2025 baseline. Where the 7-day numerical forecast shows negative root-zone water balance (< 0 mm), district agronomists and irrigation engineers should immediately coordinate supplementary irrigation through marshland pumping, river intakes, or rainwater retention dams.
guide_dashboard_matrix_desc: Data in this dashboard reflects rigorous sampling from the National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda (NISR) Seasonal Agriculture Surveys across Seasons A, B, and C. It integrates production volumes, harvested area, crop yield, and farm input adoption (inorganic fertilizers, organic manure, and improved seed varieties) to provide an authoritative baseline for agricultural policy evaluation.
guide_pilot_telemetry_desc: Continuous satellite telemetry from NASA POWER delivers solar radiation (MJ/m2/day), air temperature (°C), and atmospheric moisture demand. Daily Reference Evapotranspiration (ET0) is computed using the FAO-56 Penman-Monteith equation. The Root-Zone Water Balance (Precipitation minus ET0) provides an exact physical measure of soil moisture surplus or deficit, eliminating guesswork for irrigation scheduling.
guide_soil_terraces_title: Soil Conservation Policy & Radical Terracing Targets
guide_soil_terraces_desc: Over 75% of Rwanda agricultural land is located on hillsides with slopes exceeding 16%. In accordance with NST2 targets, land on slopes between 16° and 40° with deep soils must be protected with radical terracing, progressive terraces, and agroforestry hedgerows (such as Calliandra and Alnus) to prevent topsoil loss and preserve nutrient retention.
guide_watch_phenology_desc: This chronology connects three critical agricultural dimensions: weather anomalies (rainfall deviations vs 8-year historical baselines), crop vegetation vigor (Copernicus Sentinel-2 NDRE), and local market retail prices (WFP VAM). This multi-dimensional monitoring reveals whether production shortfalls in a district are triggering immediate price spikes in local rural markets.
guide_sim_model_desc: Unlike macro-economic forecasts, this simulation engine uses empirical coefficients derived from 28,000+ individual farming plots surveyed by NISR. By holding agroclimatic conditions constant and varying farm inputs, agronomists can estimate the specific yield gains achievable through expanded irrigation, improved seed adoption, and balanced soil fertility management.
guide_sim_ssit_desc: Under the Ministry of Agriculture and Animal Resources (MINAGRI) and Rwanda Agriculture and Animal Resources Development Board (RAB), the Government of Rwanda provides a 50% subsidy on small-scale irrigation equipment for plots up to 10 hectares. This calculator estimates the required investment for portable diesel/solar pumps, hose systems, and drip kits, comparing upfront cost against projected yield protection.
guide_advise_copilot_desc: Powered by contextual agroecological data for Rwanda five provinces, this AI Copilot assists sector agronomists, cooperative managers, and extension officers in diagnosing crop stress, calculating fertilizer requirements, scheduling irrigation cycles, and managing climate risks. Ask questions in English or Kinyarwanda.
guide_advise_ussd_desc: To ensure actionable guidance reaches smallholder farmers without smartphones or internet access, recommendations are formatted into standard 160-character mobile messages suitable for USSD and SMS push notifications through Rwanda telecommunications infrastructure (MTN & Airtel).
